clue.text: Never heard of Stonehenge? Such ignorance!

definitions.text: Never heard of Stonehenge? Such ignorance!

parts.words: Never heard of Stonehenge? Such ignorance!
parts.note: not knowing the most famous ancient stone monument in Britain would be ignorance on a colossal scale, the adjective doubling as one built from that very word

explanation.surface: Someone is scolded for never having heard of the famous stone circle.
explanation.walkthrough: Stonehenge is the prehistoric stone circle in Wiltshire, England, the archetypal ancient monument; ignorance of it is, punningly, ignorance of a monument.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossal or enormous, as in an error or ignorance so huge it seems built of stone.

clue.text: Girl married one of the most original of men

parts.words: one of the most original of men
parts.note: Abel, son of Adam and Eve, was one of the very first humans in the Bible

explanation.surface: A girl wed one of the most creative men around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original' suggests creative, but it means first: Abel was among the first men.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name.

clue.text: Late transport to bathing resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, so the letters of to bathing are sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: Evening travel to a seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like the seaside destination but means re-sort: rearrange TO BATHING.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel making an overnight crossing is transport running late at night.

clue.text: Play with chess piece — and a fine one it is

parts.note: a man is any piece in chess or draughts
super means excellent, fine
one here is another chess man

explanation.surface: A drama featuring a chess piece that is a splendid one.
explanation.walkthrough: This is George Bernard Shaw's play; 'one' repeats 'chess piece', giving a second MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedy by George Bernard Shaw, first staged in 1905.

clue.text: Pole moves, in earnest, extremely close

indicators.note: moves says one letter within earnest shifts to a new position

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for north, one of the two poles

explanation.surface: A Polish man earnestly moves very near.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person, but it is the North Pole, N; that N moves to the front of EARNEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of near, so most close or closest.

clue.text: Skilled worker removes head of old spear

indicators.note: removes head of says the first letter of the weapon's name is dropped

parts.note: a partisan is an old long-handled spear or halberd

explanation.surface: A craftsman takes the point off an antique spear.
explanation.walkthrough: The spear's 'head' looks like its metal point, but it is the first letter, P.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a craftsman, a skilled manual worker.

clue.text: Chap a ruse wrongly deprived of right

indicators.note: the words a ruse are arranged wrongly once the letter for right has been taken from them, so this phrase signals a rearrangement after a removal

explanation.surface: A man is cheated of what is rightfully his by a cunning trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly deprived of' means: take R (right) out of A RUSE and rearrange the rest. The surface fits the Bible story of Jacob tricking his brother out of his birthright.
explanation.definitionFit: Esau is a male figure from Genesis, so he is a chap, a man.

clue.text: Wise legislator not quite so prolix

indicators.note: not quite says the word for prolix falls short by its last letter

parts.note: long means lengthy and wordy, prolix

explanation.surface: A sage lawmaker who is less long-winded.
explanation.walkthrough: Solon was the lawgiver of ancient Athens, and his name now means any wise legislator.
explanation.definitionFit: Solon reformed the laws of Athens, and the name is used for any sage lawmaker.

clue.text: Lower bit of ground of secondary importance to players

parts.note: under means lower, beneath
a plot is a small piece of land

explanation.surface: A lower patch of land that matters little to sportsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'players' looks like sports players but means actors: the definition describes a subsidiary storyline in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A subplot is a secondary storyline that matters less to actors than the main one.

clue.text: Reckon first five digits, then thus contrariwise

definitions.text: Reckon first five digits, then thus
definitions.meaning: counting the fingers of one hand first, a counter then continues with the second hand
contrariwise means conversely, from the opposite point of view

explanation.surface: Instructions to count on your fingers, then the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock phrase introducing a contrasting point, and a description of counting fingers on the second hand.

clue.text: Plant one bean variety without success

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the rearranged letters go around the other piece
a variety is a different form, so the letters of one and bean are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a go is a success, as in making a go of it

explanation.surface: A gardener's single bean plant is a failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' rearranges I and BEAN into BENIA; 'without' (meaning outside) puts BENIA around GO.
explanation.definitionFit: A begonia is a flowering garden and house plant.

clue.text: Weavers' initial deception is so complicated

definitions.text: Weavers' initial deception is so complicated

parts.words: Weavers' initial deception is so complicated
parts.note: alludes to Walter Scott's line about the web we weave when first we practise to deceive, which is described as knotted and complicated

explanation.surface: A weaver's first lie spirals into complications.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is from Scott's Marmion: "Oh what a ... web we weave, when first we practise to deceive"; the weavers are liars and 'initial' is 'when first'.
explanation.definitionFit: Knotted and confused, so complicated or involved.

clue.text: Minor? Shakespeare almost was, said Jonson

definitions.text: Minor? Shakespeare almost was, said Jonson

parts.words: Minor? Shakespeare almost was, said Jonson
parts.note: Ben Jonson wrote that Shakespeare had small Latin and less Greek, so the poet was nearly without the classical language; minor itself is the Latin for less

explanation.surface: A question about Ben Jonson's verdict on Shakespeare's education.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonson's tribute says Shakespeare had "small Latine and lesse Greeke". 'Minor?' hints at Latin for 'less'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking knowledge of the classical Roman language, which Jonson suggested of Shakespeare.

clue.text: Girl found among American thieves?

definitions.meaning: a girl's name, a female first name
the proverb says there is a code of integrity among thieves, here in the US spelling

explanation.surface: A girl turns up in a gang of American crooks.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'honour among thieves' gives the second sense; 'American' signals the US spelling without the U.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, and the integrity proverbially present among thieves, in American spelling.

clue.text: King has it, rather than bishop, on board

definitions.text: King has it, rather than bishop, on board

parts.words: King has it, rather than bishop, on board
parts.note: on a chessboard the king piece is topped by a small crucifix shape while the bishop piece wears a mitre

explanation.surface: A remark about who holds a symbol of authority aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The board is a chessboard: the king piece carries a cross on its crown, the bishop has a mitre instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The crucifix shape that tops the chess king piece.

clue.text: Crowd of 100 at races

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
on means at, as in on time
a course is where races are run

explanation.surface: A hundred-strong crowd at the race meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a throng or gathering of people.

clue.text: Heavyweight sailor, oddly, applied to clipper

parts.note: a ton is a heavy weight

indicators.note: oddly says the letters of sailor are arranged in an odd way

explanation.surface: A heavy sailor gets attached to a fast sailing ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' rearranges SAILOR to SORIAL. 'clipper' looks like the sailing ship that goes with 'sailor', but it is a barber with clippers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonsorial means relating to barbers and haircutting, so it is used of someone who clips hair.

clue.text: One girl, one husband — how dull!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Nan is a girl's name
I again, the Roman numeral for one
a mate is a partner, a husband

explanation.surface: A wife's lament that her one husband is boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifeless, so lacking spirit or dull.

clue.text: Do, perhaps, daily correspondents use it?

parts.note: do is an example of a musical note in the sol-fa scale
a daily is a daily newspaper

explanation.surface: Asks whether letter writers use something every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is not the verb but the first note of the sol-fa scale (do, re, mi).
explanation.definitionFit: Writing sheets are what letter writers use.

clue.text: One central to start of project? That's right

definitions.text: One central to start of project? That's right

parts.words: One central to start of project? That's right
parts.note: the person who is key to beginning a new enterprise is a trailblazer, and the answer is built of ONE placed in the centre of a landing stage

explanation.surface: Someone key to a project's launch is confirmed.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone who starts a venture is its trailblazer; the letters also show ONE in the middle of PIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A trailblazer, the person who opens up a new field or venture.

clue.text: Formalities encountered by some gold medallists in Moscow?

definitions.text: Formalities encountered by some gold medallists in Moscow?

parts.words: Formalities encountered by some gold medallists in Moscow?
parts.note: Soviet winners at the Moscow Olympics are Reds breaking the finishing line, and the phrase also means bureaucratic procedure

explanation.surface: Bureaucracy faced by Olympic champions at the Moscow Games.
explanation.walkthrough: Moscow hosted the 1980 Olympics; a Soviet (Red) winner breaks the finishing tape.
explanation.definitionFit: Bureaucratic formalities, named after the ribbon once used to bind official papers.

clue.text: Essence of Nobel's inventive skill

parts.note: Alfred Nobel invented dynamite, a high explosive, abbreviated HE
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: What lay at the core of Alfred Nobel's talent for invention.
explanation.walkthrough: HE is the standard abbreviation for high explosive, and Nobel invented dynamite.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of something is its core or essence.

clue.text: Relatively late in life of Good Queen Bess

definitions.text: Relatively late in life of Good Queen Bess

parts.words: Relatively late in life of Good Queen Bess
parts.note: the comparative of aged describes someone later in life, and a late-life Elizabeth I would be an aged ER, the royal cipher Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A note on the later years of Elizabeth I.
explanation.walkthrough: Good Queen Bess is Elizabeth I; ER (Elizabeth Regina) is her royal cipher, so the queen late in life is OLD ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparatively aged, more advanced in years.

clue.text: Name of the French scholars or writers

parts.note: du is French for of the
MAs are Masters of Arts, scholars

explanation.surface: Asks for a name among French academics or authors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name' is part of the definition's frame: Alexandre Dumas father and son were both writers.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname shared by two French novelists, the elder and younger Alexandre.

clue.text: One of these soldiers is disciplined

definitions.text: One of these soldiers is disciplined

parts.words: One of these soldiers is disciplined
parts.note: a single soldier of this kind is an attendant, and the same word as an adjective means well-ordered and disciplined

explanation.surface: A remark that one soldier in a group is well-drilled.
explanation.walkthrough: Hospital or army attendants; the singular of the word is also an adjective meaning tidy and disciplined.
explanation.definitionFit: Military attendants who carry orders or serve officers, and in the singular, neat and well-behaved.

clue.text: Beastly party members

parts.note: male deer are beasts, and men at a pre-wedding party for the groom share the name

explanation.surface: Badly behaved guests at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag party is the British name for a groom's bachelor party.
explanation.definitionFit: Male deer, and the men attending a groom's pre-wedding night out.

clue.text: Act violently (even if a member withdraws)

definitions.text: Act violently (even if a member withdraws)

parts.words: Act violently (even if a member withdraws)
parts.note: the word means to go on a violent spree, and with the letter A and the abbreviation for a Member of Parliament removed, what remains still means to act violently

explanation.surface: Someone behaves violently even when a colleague pulls out.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A and MP (Member of Parliament) out of the answer and RAGE is left, which also means act violently.
explanation.definitionFit: To rush about violently and destructively.

clue.text: Articles at odd intervals here about Birmingham

definitions.text: Articles at odd intervals here about Birmingham

parts.words: Articles at odd intervals here about Birmingham
parts.note: the indefinite article A sits in every odd position of this word, which names the US state containing a Birmingham

explanation.surface: Newspaper articles appear irregularly in the Birmingham area.
explanation.walkthrough: Birmingham here is not the English city but the largest city of the US state. The letter A (an article) occupies positions 1, 3, 5 and 7.
explanation.definitionFit: The southern US state whose largest city is Birmingham.

clue.text: Rob with no difficulty

definitions.meaning: to relieve someone of their money, as in easing a man of his wallet

explanation.surface: A thief robs effortlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means relieve of possessions, so rob; as a noun it means facility, a lack of effort.

clue.text: Day dragging on and on without companionship

parts.note: Fri is the abbreviation for Friday
something that drags on and on seems interminable

explanation.surface: A lonely day that never seems to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no allies or pals, alone.
